title: Audit shadow-records and compact delta format for RBAC v2 admin traces
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem: Current audit capture stores either full snapshots (high storage cost) or event fragments with limited ability to reconstruct the exact state transition for complex admin operations (role inheritance, policy merges, SSO-linked changes). We need a compact, queryable representation that preserves enough context to reconstruct intent and blame, supports SAML/SSO session linking, and is amenable to redaction and tiered retention.

Goal: Design and implement an 'audit shadow-record' concept + compact delta encoding that balances fidelity, storage costs, and queryability. Shadow records are short-lived rich snapshots stored alongside compact delta streams: deltas are the canonical, queryable logs; shadow records are full materializations kept for a short retention window to accelerate reconstruction and audits. The solution should: 
- Define a stable, versioned event envelope for admin ops that includes actor, actor_confidence, target(s), pre/post diffs, session context (SAML assertion id, session id, authn_time), change intent (human/API), and optional snapshot pointers.
- Define a compact delta format (DeltaLite) optimized for role/policy trees: minimal ops, attribute-level tokenization (hashes for large blobs), and fields to support deterministic replay and blame.
- Provide canonical rules for redaction, hashing, and indexing to meet privacy and search requirements.
- Include migration strategy for existing audit consumers and dashboards (Console, Incident Runbooks, Compliance exports).

Scope: schema design, serialization format, storage TTL policy, query indexes, an API for reconstructing a change from deltas+shadow, telemetry instrumentation, and a small end-to-end prototype (ingest -> store -> reconstruct) with a follow-up rollout plan for sampling and full migration.
acceptance_criteria: Schema document published with versioning and examples for at least these admin scenarios: role assignment, role inheritance change, policy upsert, service account rotation, SSO-linked session termination.
Compact delta schema (DeltaLite) specified; examples for role tree patching and permission edge diffs included.
Prototype implementation ingests existing admin events and emits both DeltaLite and optional shadow snapshots; reconstruction API can rebuild pre/post state for test scenarios within shadow TTL.
Redaction policy documented and demoed: PII fields must be hashed or redacted in deltas while shadow snapshots can be redacted or encrypted with separate KMS keys.
Performance: write path latency increase <= 8ms p50 for typical admin ops and storage cost projection shows >= 4x reduction vs full-snapshot-only approach for long term retention tier.
Migration note and compatibility layer for Console queries and incident tooling with fallback to legacy storage for 30 days after rollout.
notes: Design constraints: queries must support: a) enumerate all actor changes affecting a target in a time window, b) reconstruct a target's state at timestamp T, c) follow policy inheritance chains for blame analysis.
We should avoid embedding large policy blobs directly in deltas. Instead store blob references and include a content-hash with the delta for integrity and caching.
SAML/SSO linkage: include saml_assertion_id, idp_entity_id, and authn_instant to assist in cross-system correlation (Confluence doc: /docs/security/sso-audit-linking).
Retention tiers: shadow_snapshot_ttl=30d by default (hot), delta_stream_retention=7y (cold). Provide configurable per-customer overrides for enterprise customers.
Privacy: PII in actor display names must be tokenized; actor identity resolution should be stored as an actor_id mapping table with separate access permissions.
Indexing: index keys: (target_id, change_time), (actor_id, change_time), (policy_hash), and a composite for role-tree-path to quickly find affected subtree changes.

Compatibility: downstream consumers (Console traces, compliance exports) must be given a small adapter library to read current events and reconstruct against shadow if available. We'll ship SDK helpers in rust/go/ts.

Storage options: DeltaLite rows stored in append-only blob store (parquet+partition) for cold tier; shadow snapshots stored in encrypted object storage with lifecycle rules and a metadata manifest in Postgres for fast lookup.
Security: shadow snapshots for high-sensitivity changes (membership of 'sys-admins') should be retained in a stricter KMS key and access-controlled vault.
Edge-case: concurrent admin ops that overlap the same role tree require deterministic ordering; include monotonic sequence id and causal vector hints in deltas.
We should coordinate with infra for throughput testing on high-change customers (sales ask: support 2000 role changes/day per org).
comments: 2026-02-22 - Liam Chen: Initial spike complete. Prototype shows ~5x storage delta vs full snapshots for sample org with 6 months of history. Need decision on the default shadow TTL.
2026-02-28 - Priya Nair (PM): Recommend TTL=30d but allow per-tenant override. Compliance export needs full snapshot option for legal requests — adding to ACs.

2026-03-02 - Security review (Mauro Silva): Approve schema shape for actor/target linking; require HMAC for blob references and audit signing for critical actions. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-07 - Design (Ellen Park): UX note: Console needs a 'reconstruct change' button that calls the reconstruction API and highlights diffs in-place. Will follow with mockups.
2026-03-10 - Liam Chen: Updated spec to include DeltaLite op set (add, remove, modify, move) and deterministic ordering rules. Ready for eng review and infra capacity planning.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal prototype and e2e tests (Q1). Phase 2: ship DeltaLite as default ingest for new admin events with shadow snapshots enabled for 10% sample of orgs (30d TTL). Phase 3: expand to 50% with tooling for Console and Compliance export adapters. Phase 4: full rollout and optional long-term snapshot export for enterprise customers. Include a migration window where legacy snapshot readers route to the adapter for 30 days.
migration_notes: Provide adapter library and migration runbook. Initial rollout will set 'legacy_reader_fallback' for 30 days; alert if reconstruction fails and escalate to oncall. We'll also provide a one-click export to legacy full-snapshot for legal holds.
qa_plan: Unit tests for schema (serialization/deserialization), fuzz tests for delta apply/rollback, integration test: ingest synthetic admin workloads and verify reconstructed state matches golden full-snapshot for 1000 random ops, performance test to validate write latency budget.
risks: Mis-indexed deltas could make targeted queries expensive; we need robust partitioning and query planning.
If shadow TTL is too short and deltas lose context (blob GC), some reconstructions will fail; must surface clear failure modes.
Encryption/key management complexity for enterprise snapshots may delay rollout; coordinate early with security infra.
Downstream consumers may assume full snapshots — adapter development is critical to avoid breakage.
